result.summary: This PR fixes the load_external_block_file fuzz target so that the shared TestingSetup chainman is fully recreated after each fuzz input is processed. Previously, LoadExternalBlockFile could add headers to the block index even when full validation failed, letting state from one fuzz input leak into subsequent inputs within the same corpus run. The change disables unused network setup so PeerManager cannot hold a stale chainman reference, and reseeds the deterministic RNG used during chainman initialization so re-initialization is itself deterministic.
result.problem: Fuzz coverage for this target was order-dependent because the shared chainman retained state (block index entries, notified header) across inputs, so results varied depending on corpus shuffling. This makes fuzzing less effective at finding and reproducing real bugs in the block-import path, a concern for anyone relying on the fuzzer for consensus-adjacent code coverage.

result.card: This PR fixes the load_external_block_file fuzz harness so the shared chainman is fully recreated after each processed input, rather than persisting state across fuzz cases. The underlying problem: LoadExternalBlockFile can add headers to the block index even when full validation fails, so reusing the chainman lets earlier fuzz inputs silently influence later ones, making corpus coverage order-dependent per the author's testing (930/930 inputs verified deterministic after the fix). This matters for test signal quality on a consensus-adjacent code path (block import), since order-dependent fuzzing can hide reproducible bugs. Review state is effectively ready: the single reviewer comment (maflcko, asking about a possible performance-only dirty-guard) was answered by the author with a substantive rationale, and no blocking issue remains.
